proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(K\) and let \(\kappa_K\) be the single constant in the premise.  Fix an arbitrary \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), and choose the asserted ambient law only to obtain its \((X,W)\) mass function \(q_a\), marginals, and operator \(A_a\).  All expectations in the first part of the proof are with respect to this design.

The bridge class is nonempty.  Indeed, the constant function \(h_{1/2}(w)=1/2\) has DCT coefficients \(\theta_1=1/2\) and \(\theta_j=0\) for \(j\ge2\), so
\[
\sum_{j=1}^K j^{2\beta}\theta_j^2=\frac14<R^2
\]
because \(R>1/2\), and \(\eta<h_{1/2}(w)<1-\eta\) because \(0<\eta<1/2\).  Thus \(h_{1/2}\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\).  The coefficient set defining \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is closed and bounded in \(\mathbb R^K\), hence compact.  The map
\[
h\longmapsto E_{q_a}\{h(W)\}
\]
is linear and continuous on this finite-dimensional set.  It therefore has a maximizer \(h_a^*\).  Define
\[
M_a=E_{q_a}\{h_a^*(W)\},
\qquad p_{0,a}(x)=(A_ah_a^*)(x).
\]
Since \(h_a^*(w)\in[\eta,1-\eta]\) for every \(w\), conditional averaging gives
\[
\eta\le p_{0,a}(x)\le1-\eta
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X_K. \tag{1}
\]

Retain the design \(q_a\) and define two full observed-data laws by
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{0,a}(X=x,W=w,Y=y)
&=q_a(x,w)p_{0,a}(x)^y\{1-p_{0,a}(x)\}^{1-y},\\
P_{t,a}(X=x,W=w,Y=y)
&=q_a(x,w)\{p_{0,a}(x)+t\}^y
  \{1-p_{0,a}(x)-t\}^{1-y},
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
where \(0<t\le\eta/2\).  By (1),
\[
\eta\le p_{0,a}(x)+t\le1-\frac\eta2. \tag{3}
\]
The cell bound \(q_a(x,w)\ge\kappa_K\), (1), and (3) imply
\[
P_{0,a}(x,w,y)\ge\kappa_K\eta,
\qquad P_{t,a}(x,w,y)\ge\frac{\kappa_K\eta}{2}, \tag{4}
\]
so both probability tables are strictly positive.  More importantly, (2) changes only the Bernoulli outcome kernel.  The \((X,W)\) law, its marginals, and \(A_a\) are unchanged.  Every member property in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) therefore follows directly from the displayed premise, with the same \(\kappa_K\) slacks.  Hence
\[
P_{0,a},P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a). \tag{5}
\]
This conclusion concerns the ambient class itself; it invokes no preservation property of any auxiliary subclass.

Under (2), the two conditional-mean functions are
\[
b_{0,a}=A_ah_a^*,
\qquad b_{t,a}=A_ah_a^*+t\mathbf 1. \tag{6}
\]
The first equality and \(h_a^*\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) give \(d(P_{0,a})=0\) by \(\mathrm{def:observable\mbox{-}defect}\).  For arbitrary \(h\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), Cauchy--Schwarz in \(L^2(q_{a,X})\), the identity \(\|\mathbf1\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}=1\), and iterated expectation yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|b_{t,a}-A_ah\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}
&\ge \left|E_{q_a}\{b_{t,a}(X)-(A_ah)(X)\}\right|\\
&=M_a+t-E_{q_a}\{h(W)\}\\
&\ge t, 
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality is the maximizing property of \(h_a^*\).  Taking \(h=h_a^*\) in (6) makes the residual equal to \(t\mathbf1\), whose norm is \(t\).  Thus
\[
d(P_{t,a})=t. \tag{8}
\]
This also gives the advertised transverse geometry.  The functional \(z\mapsto\langle z,\mathbf1\rangle_{L^2(q_{a,X})}\) exposes the maximizing face
\[
\left\{A_ah:h\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta),\ E_{q_a}h(W)=M_a\right\}
\]
of the image, (6) places \(b_{0,a}\) on that face, and \(b_{t,a}=b_{0,a}+t\mathbf1\) moves in its outward supporting-normal direction.  The maximizer cannot be an interior point of \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\): the class has nonempty interior by the strict inequalities verified for \(h_{1/2}\), and an interior maximizer could be perturbed by a sufficiently small positive multiple of \(\mathbf1\), increasing its expectation while remaining feasible.

Because of (4), \(P_{t,a}\ll P_{0,a}\).  Direct summation over \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), conditional on \(X\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})
&=E_{q_{a,X}}\!\left[
  \frac{t^2}{p_{0,a}(X)}+
  \frac{t^2}{1-p_{0,a}(X)}\right]\\
&=E_{q_{a,X}}\!\left[
  \frac{t^2}{p_{0,a}(X)\{1-p_{0,a}(X)\}}\right]\\
&\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)},
\end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
where the last step uses (1).  If \(Z=dP_{t,a}/dP_{0,a}\), then \(\log Z\le Z-1\) and change of measure imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})
&=E_{P_{t,a}}\log Z\\
&\le E_{P_{t,a}}(Z-1)
=E_{P_{0,a}}\{Z(Z-1)\}\\
&=E_{P_{0,a}}(Z-1)^2
=\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})\\
&\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}. 
\end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
The penultimate equality uses \(E_{P_{0,a}}Z=1\).

Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\mbox{-}sampling}\), product likelihood ratios factor.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
1+\chi^2(P_{t,a}^{\otimes n},P_{0,a}^{\otimes n})
&=\{1+\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})\}^n\\
&\le\exp\!\left\{n\chi^2(P_{t,a},P_{0,a})\right\}\\
&\le\exp\!\left\{\frac{nt^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}\right\},
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
which is the claimed product bound after subtracting one.

It remains to translate (11) into a testing converse.  For probability laws \(Q\ll P\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\|Q-P\|_{\rm TV}
=\frac12E_P\left|\frac{dQ}{dP}-1\right|
\le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q,P)}. \tag{12}
\]
For any possibly randomized test \(0\le\phi\le1\), the definition of total variation gives
\[
E_P\phi+E_Q(1-\phi)
=1-\{E_Q\phi-E_P\phi\}
\ge1-\|Q-P\|_{\rm TV}. \tag{13}
\]
Set
\[
c=\min\!\left\{\frac\eta2,
\sqrt{\eta(1-\eta)\log\!\left(1+(1-\epsilon_{\rm tot})^2\right)}\right\}>0,
\qquad t=\frac{c}{\sqrt n}. \tag{14}
\]
Since \(n\ge1\), (14) ensures \(0<t\le\eta/2\).  Equations (11)--(14), with \(P=P_{0,a}^{\otimes n}\) and \(Q=P_{t,a}^{\otimes n}\), yield
\[
E_{P_{0,a}^{\otimes n}}\phi+E_{P_{t,a}^{\otimes n}}(1-\phi)
\ge1-\frac{1-\epsilon_{\rm tot}}2
=\frac{1+\epsilon_{\rm tot}}2
>\epsilon_{\rm tot}. \tag{15}
\]
By (5) and (8), the first law in (15) is in the composite null and the second is in the alternative with defect \(t\).  Thus every test has total error exceeding \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\) at separation \(t\).  Monotonicity of the alternative sets in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}radius}\) proves
\[
\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge \frac{c}{\sqrt n}. \tag{16}
\]
The constant in (14) is independent of \(a\) and \(n\).  Since \(a\) was arbitrary and the same \(\kappa_K\) was assumed before choosing \(a\), (16) is uniform over \([a_L,a_U]\).  The premise also makes \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) nonempty, so combining (16) with \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\mbox{-}k\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives the asserted fixed-support equivalence.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For a fixed \(K\), suppose there is a single number \(\kappa_K>0\), chosen before \(a\), such that for every \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\) the ambient class \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) contains a law whose \((X,W)\)-marginal has mass function \(q_a\), marginals \(q_{a,X},q_{a,W}\), and conditional-expectation operator \(A_a\) satisfying
\[
\begin{gathered}
q_a(x,w)\ge \kappa_K\quad\text{for every }(x,w)\in\mathcal X_K\times\mathcal W_K,\\
q_{a,X}(x)-\frac{\eta}{K}\ge\kappa_K,
\qquad \frac{1}{\eta K}-q_{a,X}(x)\ge\kappa_K
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X_K,\\
q_{a,W}(w)-\frac{\eta}{K}\ge\kappa_K,
\qquad \frac{1}{\eta K}-q_{a,W}(w)\ge\kappa_K
\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathcal W_K,
\end{gathered}
\]
and, for every \(g\in\ell^2_{K,W}\) with \(E_{q_a}\{g(W)\}=0\),
\[
(c_{\rm link}+\kappa_K)\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}
\le \|A_ag\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}
\le (C_{\rm link}-\kappa_K)\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}.
\]
Then there are laws \(P_{0,a},P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\), having this same \((X,W)\) design and hence preserving every displayed slack, such that \(P_{0,a}\) is strictly positive, \(d(P_{0,a})=0\), and \(d(P_{t,a})=t\) for \(0<t\le\eta/2\), while
\[
D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}
\]
and
\[
\chi^2(P_{t,a}^{\otimes n},P_{0,a}^{\otimes n})
\le \exp\!\left\{\frac{nt^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}\right\}-1.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\in(0,1)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(a\) and \(n\), such that
\[
\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c n^{-1/2}.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\mbox{-}k\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), this gives \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\asymp n^{-1/2}\) uniformly in \(a\) for every fixed \(K\) satisfying the displayed common-design premise.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen premise refers to an undefined regular subclass and to several unspecified positive constants.  The narrowed premise quantifies one common slack constant before all link exponents, writes every cell, marginal, and link slack explicitly, and assumes the design directly inside the ambient class.  This is exactly what is needed to prove ambient-class membership after changing only the Bernoulli outcome kernel.

proposed.statement:
For a fixed \(K\), suppose there is a single number \(\kappa_K>0\), chosen before \(a\), such that for every \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\) the ambient class \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) contains a law whose \((X,W)\)-marginal has mass function \(q_a\), marginals \(q_{a,X},q_{a,W}\), and conditional-expectation operator \(A_a\) satisfying
\[
\begin{gathered}
q_a(x,w)\ge \kappa_K\quad\text{for every }(x,w)\in\mathcal X_K\times\mathcal W_K,\\
q_{a,X}(x)-\frac{\eta}{K}\ge\kappa_K,
\qquad \frac{1}{\eta K}-q_{a,X}(x)\ge\kappa_K
\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X_K,\\
q_{a,W}(w)-\frac{\eta}{K}\ge\kappa_K,
\qquad \frac{1}{\eta K}-q_{a,W}(w)\ge\kappa_K
\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathcal W_K,
\end{gathered}
\]
and, for every \(g\in\ell^2_{K,W}\) with \(E_{q_a}\{g(W)\}=0\),
\[
(c_{\rm link}+\kappa_K)\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}
\le \|A_ag\|_{L^2(q_{a,X})}
\le (C_{\rm link}-\kappa_K)\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}.
\]
Then there are laws \(P_{0,a},P_{t,a}\in\mathcal P_K(a)\), having this same \((X,W)\) design and hence preserving every displayed slack, such that \(P_{0,a}\) is strictly positive, \(d(P_{0,a})=0\), and \(d(P_{t,a})=t\) for \(0<t\le\eta/2\), while
\[
D_{\rm KL}(P_{t,a}\|P_{0,a})\le\frac{t^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}
\]
and
\[
\chi^2(P_{t,a}^{\otimes n},P_{0,a}^{\otimes n})
\le \exp\!\left\{\frac{nt^2}{\eta(1-\eta)}\right\}-1.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\in(0,1)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(a\) and \(n\), such that
\[
\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c n^{-1/2}.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\mbox{-}k\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), this gives \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\asymp n^{-1/2}\) uniformly in \(a\) for every fixed \(K\) satisfying the displayed common-design premise.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The explicit common-design premise introduces additional declared symbols in the statement, and the proof no longer relies on the construction-only lower-handle definition.  This replacement synchronizes the statement metadata with the narrowed claim.

prose_updates.tldr: The proposal directly tests the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\), where \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen smooth bounded diagnostic class and both the support and conditional-expectation operator are learned. A deterministic label-DCT coordinate system makes the split convex program implementable, and a finite-sample projection inequality supplies honest size and a lower confidence bound. For fixed \(K\), the root-\(n\) upper bound is matched by a transverse two-point converse whenever the ambient classes admit designs with one common positive cell, marginal, and link slack over \(a\). Under the explicit DCT compatibility condition, a legal positive-multinomial dense block also gives the \(K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) obstruction when \(K=o(n^{2/3})\) and the worst-case tail condition \(K^{-(a_L+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) holds. The complete growing-\(K\) phase diagram and valid adaptation to unknown \(a\) remain open questions.

project_justification.fill: The project supplies a deterministic-coordinate split projection upper bound, a matched fixed-support \(n^{-1/2}\) converse under an explicit ambient common-design premise, and a legal positive-multinomial dense-block lower bound of order \(K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) on the stated compatibility and worst-case-tail subregime. It leaves the operator-nuisance match, active-face calibration, complete phase diagram, adaptation factor, and maximal polynomial \(K\) range as the remaining frontier problems.

prose_updates.related_work: Wu, Fu, Wang, Wang, and Sun's Theorem 1 proves existence of a square-integrable single-NCO bridge under their causal-null, NCO, completeness, and Picard hypotheses. Those hypotheses do not imply membership in the user-chosen class \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), and no such implication is used here. Their residual tests motivate the observed-law diagnostic but do not provide the moving-image minimax frontier. Only in an application that separately stipulates that the relevant Wu bridge lies in \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) does rejection conditionally falsify that restricted causal submodel; nonrejection identifies nothing. Breunig and Chen provide the closest adaptive minimax conditional-moment method, but their separation is imposed on an NPIV structural function. Marteau and Sapatinas and Schluttenhofer and Johannes isolate signal and operator noise in diagonal Gaussian sequence experiments and therefore inform, but do not settle, the coupled multinomial problem. Chernozhukov, Newey, and Santos regularize local parameter spaces for constrained conditional moments, and Fang and Seo use projection monotonicity for fixed convex cones; the bounded image here is random and nonhomogeneous. Paninski and Chhor and Carpentier provide the legal simplex and local-probability lower-bound technology. The present dense-block result implements a common-null positive-multinomial mixture on an explicit DCT-compatible subregime, while a converse matching all operator-fitting and active-face costs remains unresolved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The formal null is the observed-law condition \(d(P)=0\); \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen statistical diagnostic class. Wu et al.'s assumptions alone do not place their bridge in this class. Rejection has a causal falsification reading only within applications that separately stipulate this restricted submodel, and nonrejection identifies nothing. The finite-sample split-projection guarantee and lower confidence bound hold over the declared union class. Fixed-support root-\(n\) sharpness additionally uses the explicit premise that the ambient classes admit \( (X,W) \) designs with one common positive cell, marginal, and link slack over \(a\). The legal dense lower bound holds under its displayed DCT compatibility condition, \(K=o(n^{2/3})\), and the uniform worst-case tail condition \(K^{-(a_L+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\); here \(a\ge a_L\) transfers that tail control to every \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\). The operator-nuisance converse, complete frontier, sharp active-face calibration, adaptation factor, and maximal polynomial \(K\) range remain open-ended questions.

statement_notes.justification: The transverse construction gives an exact-defect two-point experiment and matches the attainable root-\(n\) scale for every fixed support satisfying the explicit common-design premise.
statement_notes.gap: The converse is conditional on the ambient classes admitting \( (X,W) \) designs whose cell, marginal, and two link slacks share one positive lower bound over \(a\); it makes no claim about preserving an auxiliary regular subclass.
statement_notes.consumer: Fixed-table implementations obtain a sharp total-error benchmark, while growing-table arguments can reuse the exposed-face construction only after verifying a suitably uniform design premise.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\varepsilon\) satisfying the displayed compatibility condition.  By the definitions of the DCT bases, \(u_1=v_1=1\), the remaining basis vectors are orthogonal to the constant vector, and
\[
 |u_j(x)|\le\sqrt 2,
 \qquad
 |v_j(w)|\le\sqrt 2
 \tag{1}
\]
for every \(j\ge2\).  For fixed \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), define the joint mass function
\[
 q_a(x,w)=\frac1{K^2}\left\{1+\varepsilon\sum_{j=2}^Kj^{-a}u_j(x)v_j(w)\right\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Orthogonality to the constant vector shows that summing (2) over either coordinate gives the uniform marginal \(1/K\), and hence summing over both coordinates gives one.  Moreover, (1), \(a\ge a_L\), and the compatibility condition give
\[
 q_a(x,w)
 \ge \frac1{K^2}\left\{1-2\varepsilon\sum_{j=2}^Kj^{-a}\right\}
 \ge \frac{c_q}{K^2},
 \qquad
 c_q:=1-2\varepsilon\sum_{j=2}^{\infty}j^{-a_L}>0.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus (2) is a strictly positive probability table with \(p_X(x)=p_W(w)=1/K\).  Since \(0<\eta<1\), these marginals satisfy both balance inequalities in \(\mathcal P_K(a)\).

Under (2), the conditional mass of \(W\) given \(X=x\) is \(Kq_a(x,w)\).  DCT orthonormality therefore yields
\[
 Av_1=u_1,
 \qquad
 Av_j=\varepsilon j^{-a}u_j,
 \quad 2\le j\le K.
 \tag{4}
\]
If \(g=\sum_{j=1}^K g_jv_j\) has \(E_P\{g(W)\}=0\), uniformity of \(P_W\) implies \(g_1=0\).  Uniformity of \(P_X\), Parseval's identity, and (4) then imply
\[
 \|Ag\|_{L^2_X}^2
 =\varepsilon^2\sum_{j=2}^Kj^{-2a}g_j^2
 =\varepsilon^2\|L^{-a}g\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
Consequently the lower and upper link inequalities hold, with uniform slack
\[
 \min\{\varepsilon-c_{\rm link},\,C_{\rm link}-\varepsilon\}>0.
 \tag{6}
\]

Let \(J=\lfloor K/2\rfloor+1\), \(B_K=\{J,\ldots,K\}\), and \(m=|B_K|=K-\lfloor K/2\rfloor\).  Directly from these definitions,
\[
 K/2\le J\le K,
 \qquad
 K/2\le m\le K,
 \tag{7}
\]
so both block parameters are comparable to \(K\), including for \(K=2\).  For \(s=(s_j)_{j\in B_K}\in\{-1,1\}^m\), set
\[
 f_s(x)=\frac{\delta}{\sqrt m}\sum_{j\in B_K}s_ju_j(x).
 \tag{8}
\]
Equation (1) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \|f_s\|_\infty\le\delta\sqrt{2m}.
 \tag{9}
\]

Define \(P_0\) by the \((X,W)\) table (2) and the conditional law
\[
 P_0(Y=1\mid X=x,W=w)=\eta.
 \tag{10}
\]
The only nonzero DCT coefficient of \(h_0\equiv\eta\) is its first coefficient, equal to \(\eta\).  The standing ranges \(0<\eta<1/2\) and \(R>1/2\) imply the weak consequences
\[
 \eta\le\frac12<R,
 \qquad
 \eta\le1-\eta.
 \tag{11}
\]
It follows from (11) that \(\|L^\beta h_0\|_{\ell^2_{K,W}}=\eta\le R\) and \(\eta\le h_0(w)\le1-\eta\) for every \(w\).  Hence \(h_0\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), and its lower box constraint is active.  Constants are preserved by conditional expectation, so \(Ah_0=\eta=b_0\); therefore \(d(P_0)=0\).

For each \(s\), retain the table (2) and define \(P_s\) by
\[
 P_s(Y=1\mid X=x,W=w)=\eta+f_s(x).
 \tag{12}
\]
If \(\delta\sqrt{2m}\le\eta/2\), equations (9) and (12) show that the success probability belongs to \([\eta/2,3\eta/2]\).  Since \(\eta<1/2\), the failure probability is at least
\[
 1-\frac{3\eta}{2}>\frac14.
 \tag{13}
\]
In particular, both binary outcome probabilities under every \(P_s\), and also under \(P_0\), are at least \(\eta/2\).  Combining this fact with (3), every three-way cell has mass at least
\[
 cK^{-2},
 \qquad
 c:=c_q\eta/2>0.
 \tag{14}
\]
The outcome-kernel change in (12) leaves the two marginals and the operator \(A\) unchanged.  Equations (3)--(6) therefore verify directly that \(P_0,P_s\in\mathcal P_K(a)\); no preservation property of an unspecified subclass is being invoked.

Let \(\Pi_{B_K}\) denote the \(L^2(P_X)\)-orthogonal projection onto the span of \(\{u_j:j\in B_K\}\).  For any \(h_\theta\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), equations (4) and (7) and the source constraint give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\Pi_{B_K}Ah_\theta\|_{L^2_X}^2
 &=\varepsilon^2\sum_{j\in B_K}j^{-2a}\theta_j^2 \\
 &=\varepsilon^2\sum_{j\in B_K}j^{-2(a+\beta)}j^{2\beta}\theta_j^2 \\
 &\le\varepsilon^2J^{-2(a+\beta)}
       \sum_{j\in B_K}j^{2\beta}\theta_j^2
 \le\varepsilon^2R^2J^{-2(a+\beta)}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{15}
\]
Under \(P_s\), equation (12) gives \(b_s=\eta+f_s\), and hence \(\Pi_{B_K}b_s=f_s\).  Parseval's identity applied to (8) gives \(\|f_s\|_{L^2_X}=\delta\).  Projection contraction, the reverse triangle inequality, and (15) imply, uniformly over the complete source-and-box constrained image,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d(P_s)
 &=\inf_{h_\theta\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)}
     \|b_s-Ah_\theta\|_{L^2_X} \\
 &\ge\inf_{h_\theta\in\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)}
     \|f_s-\Pi_{B_K}Ah_\theta\|_{L^2_X} \\
 &\ge\delta-\varepsilon RJ^{-(a+\beta)}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{16}
\]

For one observation, the likelihood ratio of \(P_s\) relative to \(P_0\) is
\[
 \ell_s(O)=1+\frac{f_s(X)(Y-\eta)}{\eta(1-\eta)}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Conditioning first on \(X\), summing over the Bernoulli law (10), and using uniformity of \(P_X\) and DCT orthonormality give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_0(\ell_s\ell_t)
 &=1+\frac{\langle f_s,f_t\rangle_{L^2_X}}{\eta(1-\eta)} \\
 &=1+\frac{\delta^2}{m\eta(1-\eta)}
       \sum_{j\in B_K}s_jt_j.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{18}
\]
The amplitude restriction implies \(\delta^2<\eta(1-\eta)\), so every right-hand side in (18) is strictly positive.  Let \(\overline P=2^{-m}\sum_sP_s^{\otimes n}\).  Independence from the i.i.d. sampling assumption, the identity for the second moment of a finite likelihood-ratio mixture, and \((1+x)^n\le e^{nx}\) for \(x>-1\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 1+\chi^2(\overline P,P_0^{\otimes n})
 &=2^{-2m}\sum_{s,t}\{E_0(\ell_s\ell_t)\}^n \\
 &\le 2^{-2m}\sum_{s,t}
   \exp\!\left\{
    \frac{n\delta^2}{m\eta(1-\eta)}
    \sum_{j\in B_K}s_jt_j
   \right\} \\
 &=\cosh\!\left(\frac{n\delta^2}{m\eta(1-\eta)}\right)^m.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{19}
\]
For \(x\ge0\), \((\log\cosh x)'=\tanh x\le x\), while equality holds at zero; evenness therefore gives \(\log\cosh x\le x^2/2\) for every real \(x\).  Applying this inequality to (19) proves
\[
 \chi^2(\overline P,P_0^{\otimes n})
 \le
 \exp\!\left\{\frac{n^2\delta^4}
 {2m\eta^2(1-\eta)^2}\right\}-1.
 \tag{20}
\]

It remains to derive the minimax consequence with constants uniform in \(a\).  Choose \(c_*>0\), depending only on \(\eta\) and \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\), sufficiently small that
\[
 \frac12\left[
  \exp\!\left\{\frac{c_*^4}{2\eta^2(1-\eta)^2}\right\}-1
 \right]^{1/2}<1-\epsilon_{\rm tot},
 \tag{21}
\]
and set
\[
 \delta=c_*\frac{m^{1/4}}{\sqrt n}.
 \tag{22}
\]
If \(K=o(n^{2/3})\), then (7) and (22) imply
\[
 \delta\sqrt{2m}
 \le \sqrt2c_*\frac{K^{3/4}}{\sqrt n}=o(1),
 \tag{23}
\]
so the amplitude restriction holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).

For \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), \(J\ge K/2\), and \(K\ge2\),
\[
 J^{-(a+\beta)}
 \le 2^{a_U+\beta}K^{-(a_L+\beta)}.
 \tag{24}
\]
Choose \(c_0>0\) so small that
\[
 \varepsilon R2^{a_U+\beta}c_0
 \le c_*2^{-5/4}.
 \tag{25}
\]
Under the asserted lower-endpoint tail condition, equations (22)--(25) and \(m\ge K/2\) show that
\[
 \varepsilon RJ^{-(a+\beta)}
 \le\frac\delta2,
 \qquad
 d(P_s)\ge\frac\delta2
 \ge c_1\frac{K^{1/4}}{\sqrt n},
 \quad
 c_1:=c_*2^{-5/4}.
 \tag{26}
\]
This verifies explicitly why the condition at \(a_L\) transfers to every \(a\ge a_L\).

Substitution of (22) into (20) makes its exponent equal to \(c_*^4/[2\eta^2(1-\eta)^2]\).  Also, for any probability measures \(Q\ll P\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to their likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \|Q-P\|_{\rm TV}
 =\frac12E_P\left|\frac{dQ}{dP}-1\right|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q,P)}.
 \tag{27}
\]
Thus (20), (21), and (27) imply \(\|\overline P-P_0^{\otimes n}\|_{\rm TV}<1-\epsilon_{\rm tot}\).  For every test \(\phi\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{P_0^{\otimes n}}\phi
 +2^{-m}\sum_sE_{P_s^{\otimes n}}(1-\phi)
 &\ge1-\|\overline P-P_0^{\otimes n}\|_{\rm TV} \\
 &>\epsilon_{\rm tot}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{28}
\]
Here \(P_0\) is a valid null by (11), and every \(P_s\) is an alternative with defect at least the right-hand side of (26).  Hence no test can attain total error at most \(\epsilon_{\rm tot}\) at any separation below \(c_1K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\).  The definition of \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\) now gives the claimed lower bound, with all constants independent of \(a\), \(K\), and \(n\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume the explicit slack-compatibility condition that there is a constant \(\varepsilon\) satisfying
\[
 c_{\rm link}<\varepsilon<C_{\rm link},
 \qquad
 2\varepsilon\sum_{j=2}^{\infty}j^{-a_L}<1.
\]
There is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(a\), \(K\), and \(n\), with the following property.  For every \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\), put
\[
 J=\lfloor K/2\rfloor+1,
 \qquad
 B_K=\{J,\ldots,K\},
 \qquad
 m=|B_K|=K-\lfloor K/2\rfloor.
\]
Thus \(K/2\le J\le K\) and \(K/2\le m\le K\).  For every amplitude \(\delta>0\) satisfying \(\delta\sqrt{2m}\le\eta/2\), there are a common null law \(P_0\) and a Rademacher family \(\{P_s:s\in\{-1,1\}^m\}\) in \(\mathcal P_K(a)\) such that \(h_0\equiv\eta\) lies on the lower-box face of \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\), \(d(P_0)=0\), every \((X,W,Y)\) cell under every displayed law has mass at least \(cK^{-2}\), and the link inequalities have slack bounded away from zero uniformly in \(a\) and \(K\).  Moreover,
\[
 d(P_s)\ge \delta-\varepsilon R J^{-(a+\beta)}
\]
for every \(s\), and
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(2^{-m}\sum_sP_s^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n}\right)
 \le \exp\!\left\{\frac{n^2\delta^4}{2m\eta^2(1-\eta)^2}\right\}-1.
\]
Consequently, there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), independent of \(a\), \(K\), and \(n\), such that, whenever \(K=K_n=o(n^{2/3})\) and the worst-case tail condition
\[
 K^{-(a_L+\beta)}\le c_0\frac{K^{1/4}}{\sqrt n}
\]
holds, then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \(a\in[a_L,a_U]\),
\[
 \rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\ge c_1\frac{K^{1/4}}{\sqrt n}.
\]
The lower-endpoint tail condition suffices uniformly because \(a\ge a_L\).  This is a legal positive-multinomial dense-block converse on the displayed, explicitly nonempty compatibility subregime.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original consequence imposed its tail premise at the unknown link exponent. The adjudicated uniform result requires the stronger worst-case premise at the lower endpoint. The revised statement also exposes the amplitude condition needed for positive Bernoulli cells and records the requested block comparability and boundary checks.
